newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end up after machinery orders data.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end up after machinery orders data.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended slightly higher on Tuesday with Japan's machinery orders data, released in the afternoon, having a mixed effect on the market, traders said.
"JGBs were bought initially after the data was released, but later came down, as traders came to realise that the data was not all that weak," a trader for a trust bank's securities affiliate said.
Japan's private-sector machinery orders fell a seasonally adjusted 10.2 percent in September from the previous month, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said earlier.
The figures for September were weaker than expected and invited initial buying, traders said.
The forecast for the October-December period, however, was stronger than expected, which caused selling later on, they said.
The EPA said they expected Japan's machinery orders to rise a seasonally adjusted 19.3 percent in the October-December period.
A trader for a city bank's securities unit said JGB futures rose toward the close in sympathy with a surge in June three-month Euroyen futures.
Bids on the June Euroyen futures contract emerged after a few city banks paid fixed interest rates and received floating rates, traders said.

Some traders said these swap transactions may be related to the large issue volume of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs). About 1.1 trillion yen worth of the key CDs were traded at 0.52 percent.

The first trader said the December rose toward the close on buy-backs, as it found support near 123.45. "When the December fell to around 123.45, it gave dealers a great opportunity to buy back," the trader said.
The December ended at 123.65, up slightly from Monday's 123.55. Turnover was 42,623 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.710 percent as of 0810 GMT, down from Monday's 2.750 percent.
Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) struck a more upbeat note about economic conditions than in past months in its monthly economic report for November released this morning.

However, the JGB market's reaction was muted, as the media had already reported last week that the EPA was likely to move its assessment of current economic conditions "half a step forward" in the November report, traders said.
